bibl.title: Neural circuits in Auditory and Audiovisual Memory

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the cortical network supporting auditory and audiovisual working memory in non-human primates, and the role of ventrolateral prefrontal cortex within it
span.quote: In contrast, the ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC), which contains cells that respond robustly to auditory stimuli and that process both face and vocal stimuli may be an essential locus for both auditory and audiovisual working memory.

span.label: which cortical regions of the ventral stream are essential for non-spatial auditory working memory
span.quote: Which cortical regions within the ventral stream are essential for non-spatial auditory working memory?

span.label: argues that VLPFC is necessary for auditory and audiovisual working memory but not visual, on the strength of reversible cooling inactivation that dissociates the three
span.quote: These three experiments demonstrate that VLPFC is essential for audiovisual and auditory working memory but not for visual working memory.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: In contrast, the ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC), which contains cells that respond robustly to auditory stimuli and that process both face and vocal stimuli may be an essential locus for both auditory and audiovisual working memory.

span.label: auditory working memory
span.quote: Although there is much known about auditory pathways and processing, the underlying neural substrates of auditory working memory are poorly understood.

span.label: review
span.quote: For purposes of this review, the ability to recognize matching or nonmatching auditory stimuli, over a period of several seconds, will be considered auditory working memory.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cooling VLPFC silences a small anterolateral zone where auditory and multisensory cells are concentrated while visual cells, being spread across dorsal and ventral prefrontal cortex, keep working — producing an auditory/audiovisual deficit with visual memory spared.
span.quote: Consequently, inactivation of VLPFC affected a large proportion of auditory and multisensory cells while sparing visual neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Holding an acoustic stimulus already consumes VLPFC storage, so adding a face to remember exhausts the remaining capacity there and the extra item fails when VLPFC is inactivated.
span.quote: It is also possible that during audiovisual processing, when VLPFC is maintaining an acoustic stimulus, this burdens working memory so that adding an additional item to remember (a face) absolutely requires the remaining temporary storage in VLPFC.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Match enhancement appears earlier in prefrontal cortex than in temporal pole or primary auditory cortex, implying prefrontal top-down feedback drives the mnemonic modulation of the auditory circuit.
span.quote: The match enhancement effects observed in the PFC had an earlier latency during the matching sound presentation compared to the match enhancement seen in the dorsal temporal pole ( Ng et al., 2014 ) or in the primary auditory cortex ( Bigelow et al., 2014 ) suggesting top-down feedback is modulating the circuit during memory demand.

span.label: a live dispute about whether an entire taxon has a cognitive capacity is settled by choosing a definition, and the paper says so in those words
span.quote: Although NHP's auditory memory abilities may be less than their capacities for remembering visual information they have demonstrated the ability to discriminate and remember auditory sounds over several seconds ( Plakke et al., 2013 ), which is, by definition, auditory working memory.

span.label: the definition is not inherited but selected from among several, and the selection is announced before any evidence is reviewed
span.quote: However, for this review we will use another common definition of working memory which is “to hold an item of information ‘in-mind’ for a short period of time and to update information from moment to moment” ( Goldman-Rakic 1996 ).

span.label: and then stipulated operationally for the rest of the review, fixing what will count as an instance
span.quote: For purposes of this review, the ability to recognize matching or nonmatching auditory stimuli, over a period of several seconds, will be considered auditory working memory.

span.label: inactivation is made reversible and within-subject by cooling rather than lesioning, so each animal is its own control and the manipulation can be repeated
span.quote: We used cortical cooling to temporarily inactivate VLPFC because it can be repeated within subjects and does not harm the cortical tissue ( Lomber and Malhotra 2008 ; Yang et al., 2006 ).

span.label: memory load is reduced one modality at a time across three experiments, converting a single impairment into a dissociation
span.quote: In Experiment 2, when subjects were required to remember only the face information alone, VLPFC inactivation did not affect performance in detecting the mismatching face component ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 . In contrast, in Experiment 3, when subjects were required to remember only the vocalization, VLPFC inactivation by cooling resulted in a significant decrease in performance accuracy ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 .

span.label: the older lesion literature is discounted on two specific grounds - the lesions spanned too much cortex, and the task had no delay so it never tested working memory at all
span.quote: While these were important findings, the lesions covered a very large area of both dorsal and ventral PFC, and the task did not explicitly examine working memory, since subjects learned a conditional association without a delay.

span.label: aspiration and electrolytic lesions are noted to sever fibers of passage, so a deficit cannot distinguish damage to a region from interruption of flow through it
span.quote: Since most lesions of the primate cortex have typically been made by aspiration, or electrolytic ablation, which damage fibers of passage in addition to cells, we must look to additional lesion studies of more anterior auditory cortical regions.

span.label: latency ordering across regions is used to infer direction of influence, with match enhancement appearing earlier in prefrontal cortex than in temporal pole or auditory cortex
span.quote: In fact, single cells track which particular component changed, whether the nonmatch was a change in the face or voice component, Figure 3 ( Hwang and Romanski 2015 ).

span.label: the anatomical explanation for the dissociation is concentration: auditory cells are clustered in one small area while visual cells are spread across the whole prefrontal cortex
span.quote: Consequently, inactivation of VLPFC affected a large proportion of auditory and multisensory cells while sparing visual neurons.

span.label: an alternative reading of the same dissociation is offered in terms of capacity rather than locus - cooling may bite only when the store is already burdened
span.quote: It is also possible that during audiovisual processing, when VLPFC is maintaining an acoustic stimulus, this burdens working memory so that adding an additional item to remember (a face) absolutely requires the remaining temporary storage in VLPFC. For this reason, when VLPFC is inactivated performance declines.

span.label: tract tracing from acoustically characterised cortex establishes that the projections exist before any functional claim is made
span.quote: The areas of the temporal lobe implicated in auditory memory processing project to the prefrontal cortex ( Barbas 1992 ; Petrides and Pandya 1988 ; Plakke and Romanski 2014 ; Romanski et al., 1999a ; Romanski and Averbeck 2009 )

span.label: The equivalent auditory working-memory recordings have not yet been made in VLPFC itself
span.note: what this limits: any claim about VLPFC in auditory working memory: IDENTICAL STUDIES OF AUDITORY WORKING MEMORY HAVE YET TO BE CONDUCTED IN VLPFC
span.quote: Identical studies of auditory working memory have yet to be conducted in VLPFC, although, it has been shown that VLPFC neurons respond to both stimulus and task variables in an audiovisual working memory task ( Hwang and Romanski 2015 ).

span.label: The division of labour between the implicated cortical regions is not yet settled
span.note: what this limits: the division of labour between the regions: DELINEATING THE PRECISE ROLE THAT IS PLAYED BY EACH OF THESE CORTICAL REGIONS IN ENCODING, MAINTENANCE, AND RETRIEVAL OF AUDITORY STIMULI IS AN ONGOING ENDEAVOR
span.quote: Delineating the precise role that is played by each of these cortical regions in encoding, maintenance, and retrieval of auditory stimuli is an ongoing endeavor.

span.label: Current techniques lack the resolution needed to trace information flow during auditory mnemonic processing
span.note: what this limits: any claim about information FLOW: TECHNIQUES WITH BETTER TEMPORAL RESOLUTION AND SPATIAL SPECIFICITY ARE NEEDED TO DETERMINE THE PRECISE NATURE OF INFORMATION FLOW DURING AUDITORY MNEMONIC PROCESSING
span.quote: Clearly, techniques with better temporal resolution and spatial specificity are needed to determine the precise nature of information flow during auditory mnemonic processing.

span.label: The mapping between forms of auditory memory and their circuits remains open
span.note: what this limits: the mapping from memory type to circuit: THE VARIOUS FORMS OF AUDITORY MEMORY (WORKING, SHORT-TERM, LONG-TERM) AND THE PRECISE NEURONAL CIRCUITS THAT EACH FORM OF MEMORY RELIES ON, IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION
span.quote: The various forms of auditory memory (working, short-term, long-term) and the precise neuronal circuits that each form of memory relies on, is still under investigation.

span.label: the animal model itself has been the bottleneck for the whole question
span.note: what this limits: the whole literature's pace: HISTORICALLY, PART OF THE PROBLEM HAS BEEN THE DIFFICULTY IN OBTAINING A ROBUST ANIMAL MODEL TO STUDY AUDITORY SHORT-TERM MEMORY
span.quote: Historically, part of the problem has been the difficulty in obtaining a robust animal model to study auditory short-term memory.

span.label: the neural substrates remain poorly understood despite extensive knowledge of auditory pathways
span.note: what this limits: the gap between pathway anatomy and function: ALTHOUGH THERE IS MUCH KNOWN ABOUT AUDITORY PATHWAYS AND PROCESSING, THE UNDERLYING NEURAL SUBSTRATES OF AUDITORY WORKING MEMORY ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD
span.quote: Although there is much known about auditory pathways and processing, the underlying neural substrates of auditory working memory are poorly understood.

span.label: which circuits serve which form of auditory memory is unresolved
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[3] · what this limits: the same scope as item 3 - which circuit serves which form of memory
span.quote: The various forms of auditory memory (working, short-term, long-term) and the precise neuronal circuits that each form of memory relies on, is still under investigation.

span.label: the division of labour among temporal regions is not yet established
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[1] · what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - the regional division of labour
span.quote: Delineating the precise role that is played by each of these cortical regions in encoding, maintenance, and retrieval of auditory stimuli is an ongoing endeavor.

span.label: current techniques lack the resolution the question needs
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[2] · what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - resolution limits on information-flow claims
span.quote: Clearly, techniques with better temporal resolution and spatial specificity are needed to determine the precise nature of information flow during auditory mnemonic processing.

span.label: the DLPFC recordings are hard to interpret because responses there track task rather than stimulus type
span.note: what this limits: the DLPFC recordings: RESPONSES IN DLPFC APPEAR TO BE MORE TASK-RELATED AND LESS DEPENDENT ON TYPE OF STIMULI
span.quote: However, responses in DLPFC appear to be more “task-related” and less dependent on type of stimuli.

span.label: training non-human primates on auditory tasks takes far longer than on matched visual tasks, which shapes which experiments exist at all
span.note: what this limits: which experiments exist at all: IT TYPICALLY TAKES LONGER TO TRAIN NHPs TO LEARN AN AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION OR MEMORY TASK THAN TO LEARN A SIMILAR TASK USING VISUAL STIMULI
span.quote: It typically takes longer to train NHPs to learn an auditory discrimination or memory task than to learn a similar task using visual stimuli ( D'Amato and Salmon 1984 ; Fritz et al., 2005 ; Hashiya and Kojima 2001 ).

span.label: the delayed match-to-sample paradigm and the match enhancement/suppression indices, carried across to audition where the tasks proved far harder to train
span.quote: It typically takes longer to train NHPs to learn an auditory discrimination or memory task than to learn a similar task using visual stimuli ( D'Amato and Salmon 1984 ; Fritz et al., 2005 ; Hashiya and Kojima 2001 ).

span.label: call-sequence comprehension in the wild, used as evidence that primates possess auditory memory before any laboratory task is invoked
span.quote: For example, if a Campbell's monkey makes an alarm call for an eagle, Diana monkeys will also produce alarm calls signaling eagles, however, if a boom vocalization occurs before the alarm call of the Campbell monkey the Diana monkeys ignores the warning ( Zuberbuhler 2002 ). The boom vocalization changes the meaning of the subsequent alarm call, and the Diana monkeys recognize this context and do not send out their own alarm calls.

span.label: reversible cooling deactivation, and the dorsal/ventral dissociation it produced, imported as both method and expected result pattern
span.quote: For example, Lomber & Malhotra (2008) dissociated the function of auditory cortical regions when they showed that inactivation of the anterior auditory field, AAF, in cats impaired auditory pattern discrimination, while lesions of area DP, a hypothesized dorsal stream region, impaired sound localization ( Lomber and Malhotra 2008 ).

span.label: ventrolateral PFC
span.quote: with the dorsolateral PFC performing similar functions for both auditory and visual working memory. In contrast, the ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC), which contains cells that respond robustly to auditory stimuli and that process both face and vocal stimuli may be an essential locus for both auditory and audiovisual working memory

span.label: dorsolateral PFC
span.quote: with the dorsolateral PFC performing similar functions for both auditory and visual working memory. In contrast, the ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC), which contains cells that respond robustly to auditory stimuli and that process both face and vocal stimuli may be an essential locus for both auditory and audiovisual working memory

span.label: working memory - as the Baddeley multi-component system versus as Goldman-Rakic hold-and-update; the review names both and picks the second
span.quote: One classic definition describes working memory as a method to control attention through the ‘central executive’, composed of the visuospatial sketchpad, phonological loop, and ‘episodic buffer’ ( Baddeley and Hitch 1974 ; Baddeley 2000 ).

span.label: working memory - the chosen definition stated in full, which is what makes the rest of the review's evidence admissible
span.quote: However, for this review we will use another common definition of working memory which is “to hold an item of information ‘in-mind’ for a short period of time and to update information from moment to moment” ( Goldman-Rakic 1996 ).

span.label: auditory working memory in monkeys - as a genuine capacity versus as passive short-term memory; a disagreement about a taxon that turns on which term applies
span.quote: It has been suggested that nonhuman primates (NHPs) do not have auditory working memory ( Scott et al., 2012 ; Scott et al., 2013 ), but possess a much more limited short-term mnemonic ability termed ‘passive short-term memory’.

span.label: auditory working memory - stipulated operationally for this review, fixing what counts as an instance of it
span.quote: For purposes of this review, the ability to recognize matching or nonmatching auditory stimuli, over a period of several seconds, will be considered auditory working memory.

span.label: auditory memory - recognising the TYPE of a sound (intact) versus recalling the specific sound heard (impaired); one task splitting into two capacities
span.quote: Interestingly, when participants were asked to identify the sound clip (e.g. Dog bark) they could do so, indicating that long-term storage to recognize sound type was intact, but the ability to recall the specific sound they had previously heard was still impaired.

span.label: forgetting - by decay with time versus by interference from other items; both argued to operate once rehearsal is controlled
span.quote: It has been suggested that interference may play a greater role in decreased auditory memory performance than decay ( Lewandowsky et al., 2008 ), but a recent study examining memory for timbre found that decay does play a role in memory performance when both interference and rehearsal are controlled for ( McKeown and Mercer 2012 ).

span.label: match response - enhancement in prefrontal cortex versus suppression in temporal regions, one recognition event with opposite signs
span.quote: Similar effects have been observed for visual working memory with more match enhancement in prefrontal regions ( Miller et al., 1996 ) and match suppression occurring in temporal lobe regions ( Miller et al., 1993 ).

span.label: claim_type: mechanism
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: These findings suggest a critical role for the VLPFC in the processing, integrating, and retaining of communication information.

span.label: method: review of lesion, neurophysiological and neuroimaging work, culminating in the authors' own reversible cortical cooling of VLPFC during an audiovisual delayed nonmatch-to-sample task
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: review — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: We used cortical cooling to temporarily inactivate VLPFC because it can be repeated within subjects and does not harm the cortical tissue ( Lomber and Malhotra 2008 ; Yang et al., 2006 ).

span.label: phenomenon: auditory working memory - holding and updating recently heard sounds over seconds
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: auditory working memory — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Working memory is the ability to employ recently seen or heard stimuli and apply them to changing cognitive context.

span.label: contradicts → Scott et al., 2012; Scott et al., 2013 (claim that non-human primates lack auditory working memory)
span.quote: Although NHP's auditory memory abilities may be less than their capacities for remembering visual information they have demonstrated the ability to discriminate and remember auditory sounds over several seconds ( Plakke et al., 2013 ), which is, by definition, auditory working memory.

span.label: extends → Hwang and Romanski (2015)
span.quote: In order to examine this question we trained non-human primates in the same audiovisual delayed nonmatch-to-sample paradigm as utilized by Hwang and Romanski (2015) and temporally inactivated the VLPFC ( Plakke et al., 2015 ).

span.label: builds-on → Plakke et al. (2015) VLPFC cooling inactivation experiments
span.quote: The inactivation experiments in Plakke et al., (2015) provides direct evidence that VLPFC is an essential region for auditory working memory and suggests VLPFC is a major end point of the auditory ventral stream, necessary for auditory cognition.

span.label: contradicts → Scott et al. (2012, 2013), that non-human primates lack auditory working memory and have only passive short-term memory
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER THE DEMONSTRATED ABILITY MEETS THE DEFINITION. 'ALTHOUGH NHP'S AUDITORY MEMORY ABILITIES MAY BE LESS THAN THEIR CAPACITIES FOR REMEMBERING VISUAL INFORMATION they have demonstrated the ability to DISCRIMINATE AND REMEMBER AUDITORY SOUNDS OVER SEVERAL SECONDS, WHICH IS, BY DEFINITION, AUDITORY WORKING ME[MORY].' The weaker performance is conceded and the categorical claim is refused on definitional grounds - so the disagreement is about whether a smaller capacity is still the same faculty. Q-513.
span.quote: Although NHP's auditory memory abilities may be less than their capacities for remembering visual information they have demonstrated the ability to discriminate and remember auditory sounds over several seconds ( Plakke et al., 2013 ), which is, by definition, auditory working memory.

span.label: critiques → the early prefrontal lesion studies, for lesions spanning too much cortex and for a task with no delay
span.quote: While these were important findings, the lesions covered a very large area of both dorsal and ventral PFC, and the task did not explicitly examine working memory, since subjects learned a conditional association without a delay.

span.label: critiques → aspiration and electrolytic lesion methods generally, which cannot separate damage to a region from interruption of fibers passing through it
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER FIBRES OF PASSAGE ARE DAMAGED. 'Since MOST LESIONS OF THE PRIMATE CORTEX HAVE TYPICALLY BEEN MADE BY ASPIRATION, OR ELECTROLYTIC ABLATION, WHICH DAMAGE FIBERS OF PASSAGE IN ADDITION TO CELLS, we must look to additional lesion studies.' A whole generation of results cannot distinguish removing a region from cutting what runs through it - and the critique applies to the technique, so it lands on every study that used it regardless of what each found. Q-507.
span.quote: Since most lesions of the primate cortex have typically been made by aspiration, or electrolytic ablation, which damage fibers of passage in addition to cells, we must look to additional lesion studies of more anterior auditory cortical regions.

span.label: extends → Hwang and Romanski (2015), from correlational single-unit responses to a necessity claim via inactivation
span.quote: Inactivation of VLPFC, by cooling, resulted in a significant impairment on both auditory mismatch and visual mismatch trials, indicating that VLPFC is necessary for audiovisual working memory ( Figure 5 ).

span.label: builds-on → Romanski and Goldman-Rakic, that VLPFC neurons respond to complex sounds and species-specific vocalizations but not to simple stimuli
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS STIMULUS COMPLEXITY. 'IN COMPARISON TO RESPONSES OF NEURONS IN DLPFC, SINGLE NEURONS IN VLPFC RESPOND ROBUSTLY TO COMPLEX SOUNDS, INCLUDING SPECIES-SPECIFIC VOCALIZATIONS BUT NOT TO SIMPLE STIMULI.' A region characterised by what it does NOT respond to as much as by what it does - so a study using tones would find VLPFC silent and conclude it is not auditory. Q-513.
span.quote: In comparison to responses of neurons in DLPFC, single neurons in VLPFC respond robustly to complex sounds, including species-specific vocalizations but not to simple stimuli ( Romanski and Goldman-Rakic 2002 ).

span.label: supports → the body of single-unit and neuroimaging work implicating ventral PFC in auditory working memory
span.quote: The inactivation experiments in Plakke et al., (2015) provides direct evidence that VLPFC is an essential region for auditory working memory and suggests VLPFC is a major end point of the auditory ventral stream, necessary for auditory cognition.

span.label: auditory working memory —contrasted-with→ passive short-term memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: It has been suggested that nonhuman primates (NHPs) do not have auditory working memory ( Scott et al., 2012 ; Scott et al., 2013 ), but possess a much more limited short-term mnemonic ability termed ‘passive short-term memory’.

span.note: strength of the relation: 1

span.quote: One classic definition describes working memory as a method to control attention through the ‘central executive’, composed of the visuospatial sketchpad, phonological loop, and ‘episodic buffer’ ( Baddeley and Hitch 1974 ; Baddeley 2000 ).

span.quote: These three experiments demonstrate that VLPFC is essential for audiovisual and auditory working memory but not for visual working memory.

span.quote: The inactivation experiments in Plakke et al., (2015) provides direct evidence that VLPFC is an essential region for auditory working memory and suggests VLPFC is a major end point of the auditory ventral stream, necessary for auditory cognition.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Similar effects have been observed for visual working memory with more match enhancement in prefrontal regions ( Miller et al., 1996 ) and match suppression occurring in temporal lobe regions ( Miller et al., 1993 ).

span.label: delay suppression —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85
span.quote: Delay suppression, thought to represent a form of active maintenance, has also been observed in human auditory cortex when participants were remembering auditory stimuli ( Linke et al., 2011 ).

span.label: RETRACTED (THE `from` ENDPOINT IS OVER-SPECIFIED AND UNATTESTED) · decay —contrasted-with→ proactive interference
span.note: RETRACTED: THE `from` ENDPOINT IS OVER-SPECIFIED AND UNATTESTED. The edge is `decay --contrasted-with--> proactive interference`. The span: 'It has been suggested that INTERFERENCE MAY PLAY A GREATER ROLE IN DECREASED AUDITORY MEMORY PERFORMANCE THAN DECAY (Lewandowsky et al., 2008), but a recent study examining memory for timbre found that DECAY DOES PLAY A ROLE.' The contrast is real and well drawn - interference against decay, with a citation on each side - AND THE SPAN SAYS `INTERFERENCE`, NOT `PROACTIVE INTERFERENCE`. Proactive interference is a specific kind, distinguished in this literature from retroactive; the qualifier was supplied. TRUE OF THE FIELD, NOT IN THE SPAN, and the endpoint test caught it where reading past it would not have. Q-433. — strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: It has been suggested that interference may play a greater role in decreased auditory memory performance than decay ( Lewandowsky et al., 2008 ), but a recent study examining memory for timbre found that decay does play a role in memory performance when both interference and rehearsal are controlled for ( McKeown and Mercer 2012 ).

span.label: face cells —part-of→ multisensory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.75
span.quote: Noting that these “face cells” were located within the same regions as vocalization responsive auditory cells, Romanski and colleagues demonstrated that a large proportion of VLPFC neurons are multisensory and respond to faces and vocalizations ( Diehl and Romanski 2014 ; Romanski and Hwang 2012 ; Sugihara et al., 2006 ).

span.label: ventrolateral prefrontal cortex —contrasted-with→ dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: In comparison to responses of neurons in DLPFC, single neurons in VLPFC respond robustly to complex sounds, including species-specific vocalizations but not to simple stimuli ( Romanski and Goldman-Rakic 2002 ).

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: In comparison to responses of neurons in DLPFC, single neurons in VLPFC respond robustly to complex sounds, including species-specific vocalizations but not to simple stimuli ( Romanski and Goldman-Rakic 2002 ).

span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS the record's ventrolateral/dorsolateral edge, whose span named neither endpoint. The paper states the contrast using ABBREVIATIONS; `normalised` maps them onto the full names the record already carries.
span.quote: with the dorsolateral PFC performing similar functions for both auditory and visual working memory. In contrast, the ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC), which contains cells that respond robustly to auditory stimuli and that process both face and vocal stimuli may be an essential locus for both auditory and audiovisual working memory

span.label: Cooling the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex significantly impaired detection of both auditory and visual mismatches when monkeys had to hold a face-voice pair in memory.
span.quote: Inactivation of VLPFC, by cooling, resulted in a significant impairment on both auditory mismatch and visual mismatch trials, indicating that VLPFC is necessary for audiovisual working memory ( Figure 5 ).

span.label: When only the face had to be remembered, VLPFC cooling left performance intact.
span.quote: In Experiment 2, when subjects were required to remember only the face information alone, VLPFC inactivation did not affect performance in detecting the mismatching face component ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 .

span.label: When only the vocalization had to be remembered, VLPFC cooling significantly reduced accuracy, even at a delay of only about a second.
span.quote: In contrast, in Experiment 3, when subjects were required to remember only the vocalization, VLPFC inactivation by cooling resulted in a significant decrease in performance accuracy ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 .

span.label: Across the three cooling experiments VLPFC proved necessary for auditory and audiovisual working memory but dispensable for visual working memory.
span.quote: These three experiments demonstrate that VLPFC is essential for audiovisual and auditory working memory but not for visual working memory.

span.label: The inactivation results place VLPFC as a necessary endpoint of the auditory ventral stream for auditory cognition rather than merely a correlated node.
span.quote: The inactivation experiments in Plakke et al., (2015) provides direct evidence that VLPFC is an essential region for auditory working memory and suggests VLPFC is a major end point of the auditory ventral stream, necessary for auditory cognition.

span.label: Visually responsive prefrontal neurons are distributed across both dorsal and ventral prefrontal cortex, whereas auditory-responsive cells are confined to VLPFC.
span.quote: On the other hand, there are unimodal visual responsive neurons, found across a wide region of both dorsal and ventral prefrontal cortex; these cells are not confined to VLPFC as auditory responsive cells are.

span.label: Anterior auditory belt regions project to the frontal pole and to ventrolateral prefrontal areas 12vl, 12 orbital and 45, giving VLPFC direct access to non-spatial acoustic information.
span.quote: Anterior auditory belt and parts of ML show strong projections to the frontal pole, the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex areas 12 vl, 12 orbital and 45 (i.e. inferior convexity), and the rostral principle sulcus ( Romanski et al., 1999b ).

span.label: Caudal auditory cortex, which codes sound location, targets a different frontal set: the caudal principal sulcus, frontal eye fields and dorsal premotor cortex.
span.quote: In contrast, caudal auditory cortical regions, which respond to sound location, project to the caudal principal sulcus, frontal eye fields and dorsal premotor cortex.

span.label: Memory for sounds is weaker than memory for images: auditory memory decays faster and is more easily disrupted by interference than visual memory.
span.quote: Comparisons of auditory and visual memory curves highlight the notion that auditory memory is more susceptible to interference and less robust compared to visual memory ( Wright 2007 ).

span.label: What degrades auditory memory is chiefly distraction during the retention interval rather than the sheer duration of the delay.
span.quote: This suggests that during auditory memory, distraction occurring during the delay, may be more important than the length of the delay itself

span.label: cooling VLPFC impaired both auditory and visual mismatch detection when both components had to be held
span.quote: Inactivation of VLPFC, by cooling, resulted in a significant impairment on both auditory mismatch and visual mismatch trials, indicating that VLPFC is necessary for audiovisual working memory ( Figure 5 ).

span.label: with only the face to remember, cooling VLPFC did nothing; with only the vocalization, it impaired performance
span.quote: In Experiment 2, when subjects were required to remember only the face information alone, VLPFC inactivation did not affect performance in detecting the mismatching face component ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 . In contrast, in Experiment 3, when subjects were required to remember only the vocalization, VLPFC inactivation by cooling resulted in a significant decrease in performance accuracy ( Plakke et al., 2015 ), Figure 6 .

span.label: the auditory deficit appeared at a delay as short as 1.25 seconds
span.quote: This auditory working memory deficit occurred in both subjects at a relatively short (1.25 second) delay, indicating that the prefrontal cortex may be more important for maintaining auditory information in memory than visual.

span.label: monkeys remember fewer auditory than visual items
span.quote: He showed that monkeys could not remember as many auditory items as visual items.

span.label: auditory memory is more susceptible to interference and less robust than visual memory
span.quote: Comparisons of auditory and visual memory curves highlight the notion that auditory memory is more susceptible to interference and less robust compared to visual memory ( Wright 2007 ).

span.label: humans show steeper forgetting curves for auditory than visual material, as monkeys do
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated - 2026-08-26 terminal-a.
